name: chalk-snap
title: Chalk Snap
description: A freehand annotation layer over any UI, doc, or code region: every pointer stroke quantizes live onto an invisible character grid as box-drawing glyphs, so scribbling produces a real, copyable ASCII diagram instead of a screenshot.
useWhen: a human is marking up an existing UI, doc, or code region by hand and the point is capturing that gesture as pasteable plain text — dragging quantizes the stroke live onto the grid, with hysteresis so hand wobble doesn't flicker the glyph, and a copy action emits the raster anywhere a screenshot can't go (an issue, a PR comment, a terminal). Pick diagram-ascii-flow instead when the graph already exists as data (nodes/edges) and the job is rendering and re-routing it, not capturing a freehand gesture — that component is post-hoc conversion, this one is real-time capture.
instruction: Wraps `children` (the UI/doc/code region being annotated — optional, omit for a blank grid sized by `cols`/`rows`) with an invisible cell grid measured off the real font metrics: a hidden 1ch x 1lh probe span plus a ResizeObserver on the host (same idiom as container-box-drawing), so the grid always tiles to whole characters over whatever content sits underneath, no assumed pixel size. THE MECHANISM: on pointerdown the grid captures the pointer and starts a walk; on every pointermove, `walkTo` converts the continuous pointer position into a discrete cell-by-cell walk toward it, one grid step per iteration, choosing between the horizontal and vertical axis with a hysteresis margin (a committed axis keeps winning unless the other axis's delta beats it by more than HYSTERESIS) — this is what stops a hand that's basically drawing a straight line from flickering the glyph between ─ and │ on every wobble pixel. Each committed step OR-accumulates a 4-bit N/E/S/W direction mask into a shared `Map<'x,y', mask>` covering every stroke ever drawn (never reset except by Clear), and a 16-entry lookup table turns any accumulated mask into its box-drawing character: straight runs (─│), corners (┌┐└┘), three-way junctions (├┤┬┴), and the four-way crossing (┼) — so two strokes that cross or meet resolve their junction from neighbor bits alone, no separate pass. A stroke's trailing pointer speed is smoothed (exponential, 0.6/0.4) across pointermove events; if it clears ARROW_VELOCITY at pointerup, the final cell gets an arrowhead (► ◄ ▲ ▼) in the direction of travel instead of a plain rule. SETTLE: every cell whose mask (or arrow) actually changes bumps its own generation counter, which is folded into that glyph span's React `key` — the remount replays a 220ms ease-out-expo (`cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`) keyframe that scales and translates in from CSS custom properties holding the raw pointer offset at the moment that cell committed, back to the cell's true center, so the glyph visibly snaps from where the hand actually was to where the grid disciplined it. TRAIL: an SVG polyline of the raw, unsnapped pointer path renders in `--ns-accent` while a stroke is active, then fades over ~200ms after pointerup before its points are cleared — the accent color never touches settled ink, only the live gesture and the keyboard cursor. KEYBOARD: the grid is one focusable region (a real aria-label states every control). Arrow keys move a visible `--ns-accent`-outlined cursor cell, shown only while the region has focus. Shift+Arrow commits one segment through the identical `applyBit` path pointer strokes use, grouping consecutive shift-moves into one open run; a plain arrow move (or Escape) closes that run without an arrowhead, Enter caps it with one in its last direction. A11Y: the glyph raster and the raw trail are both `aria-hidden` — box-drawing glyphs read character-by-character by a screen reader are noise, not signal. A visually-hidden `<ul>` is the shadow description instead: one line per completed stroke, plain language ('arrow from row 3 col 10 to row 3 col 42' / 'line from row 1 col 4 to row 5 col 4'), kept in sync by the same `recordStroke` call both pointer and keyboard paths use. `Copy raster` builds the plain-text grid (trailing whitespace trimmed per row) and writes it via the Clipboard API; the result — success, empty-grid no-op, or failure — lands in a `role=status aria-live=polite` region since the write is async. `Clear` resets the grid, the trail, and the stroke log in one action. Every color is a token (`--foreground` for settled ink, `--ns-accent` for the live trail and cursor only, `--border`/`--ns-muted` for chrome) — no hex. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes the settle keyframe and the trail/cursor transitions; the grid, the walk, and the copy/clear controls stay fully usable with instant state changes instead of animated ones. Pure DOM + CSS + a transient SVG path — no canvas.
